documented.text: The shopper pays with a card saved in the Agentcard Vault. After the shopper approves, Agentcard places the order with that card. max_charge is the most the card can be held for.
The shopper approves each payment on a link that works for about 15 minutes. The amount shown is the cart's max_charge, the most the card can be held for.

An auto-approval rule, or the app's permission, can pay without an approval link only when the store's processor fixes the amount, the checkout page is on the store the shopper said yes to, and the amount is within the rule's limits or the app's permission.

The Vault text says the app can pay without asking the user here. It states no spending limit or end date, and the user can turn this off anytime in the Vault. Agentcard does not check that the app asked the user before each purchase.
Every other purchase, including at a Shopify store, sends the approval link. A store that turns the card into a token can charge that token later for any amount.

documented.text: The MCP server page says the agent trades inside a dedicated Agentic sub-account, isolated from the main account. The sub-account type is Agentic virtual sub. The owner funds that sub-account manually in the web UI. The agent cannot pull funds from the main account.

Scopes chosen at connect are Market data, Account, Trade, and Transfer. Transfer moves funds between wallets inside the same sub-account only. There is no withdrawal scope, so the agent cannot move funds to an external address.

The MCP server page says the agent restates each order, cancel, and transfer and waits for the user's yes before sending it. The page calls this confirm before execute. It applies to every non-read action.
